paragraphs.en: The Sunday Scaries Are Real—And They're Getting Worse
paragraphs.cn: 周日焦虑确实存在——而且愈发严重

paragraphs.en: Jill Davis's official work week starts Monday morning. Unofficially, it kicks off every Sunday afternoon when, like clockwork, anxious thoughts begin seeping into her brain.
paragraphs.cn: 吉尔·戴维斯的正式工作周从周一早上开始。但实际上，她的工作周从每周日下午就开始了——那时，焦虑的念头便如时钟般准时地涌入她的脑海。

paragraphs.en: "Am I organized and ready enough? Am I prepared for this meeting?" says Davis, the chief development officer at a nonprofit. To bat the angst away, she'll often launch into work, writing emails and saving them as drafts so she doesn't disturb her colleagues.
paragraphs.cn: “我是否安排妥当、准备充分？我为这次会议做好准备了吗？”这家非营利组织的发展总监戴维斯说道。为了驱散焦虑，她通常会立刻开始工作，撰写邮件并保存为草稿，这样就不会打扰到同事。

paragraphs.en: Chances are they're already fretting about work, too. The "Sunday scares" have become such a fixture of Americans' weekends that Merriam-Webster added the term to its online dictionary last month. Its definition: a feeling of anxiety or sadness one may feel when the weekend is almost over, either because the work/school week is about to begin, there is no more time for fun or relaxing weekend activities, or both.
paragraphs.cn: 很可能他们也已经在为工作发愁了。“周日焦虑”如今已成为美国人周末时的常态，以至于《韦氏词典》上个月将这一术语纳入其在线词典。其定义为：当周末即将结束时，人们因即将迎来工作/上学周、再也没有时间享受休闲娱乐活动，或两者兼而有之而产生的焦虑或悲伤情绪。

paragraphs.en: That pre-Monday dread isn't a new phenomenon, but there's reason to believe it is intensifying as workloads mount and job security ebbs. More than half of U.S. workers say they experience
paragraphs.cn: 那种周一前的焦虑感并非新鲜现象，但有理由相信，随着工作负担加重且工作稳定性下降，这种情绪正日益严重。超过半数的美国劳动者表示他们会有这种体验。
